solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Peppered with bullets, fell with audible groan

indicators.note: audible says the word for groan is to be taken as heard, not as spelt

parts.note: to groan is to moan
a fell is a hill or moor, as is a down (the South Downs)

explanation.surface: Someone collapses with a moan after being riddled with gunfire.
explanation.walkthrough: 'fell' looks like a verb but is the noun: a fell and a down are both open upland.
explanation.definitionFit: To be cut down by gunfire, killed or felled en masse, is a phrasal-verb idiom for being riddled with bullets.

clue.text: Confusion, note, with Henry stopping tennis shot

parts.note: mi is a note of the sol-fa scale

indicators.note: stopping means plugging, so the Henry letter goes inside

parts.note: a smash is an overhead tennis shot
H is the unit henry in physics

explanation.surface: A tennis rally descends into chaos when Henry blocks a shot.
explanation.definitionFit: A mishmash is a confused jumble, a synonym of confusion.

clue.text: Cleans socks son initially removed

indicators.note: initially removed says the son letter goes from the front

parts.note: socks means hits, swipes

explanation.surface: A boy's socks are washed, starting with taking them off.
explanation.walkthrough: 'socks' looks like hosiery but is the verb, hits.
explanation.definitionFit: To wipe is to clean by rubbing, so wipes means cleans.

clue.text: TV boss recording late broadcast with extremely rude content

indicators.note: content means contained, so the outer letters of rude go inside
broadcast means scattered abroad, so the letters are jumbled
extremely means the outside letters of rude

explanation.surface: A late broadcast with crude material lands on the TV chief's desk.
explanation.walkthrough: 'broadcast' rearranges RECORDING LATE; 'content' takes RE (the ends of rude) inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: The Director-General heads the BBC, the British public broadcaster, so a TV boss.

clue.text: Expert such as Hadrian, hero of the Scots

parts.note: Hadrian's Wall is the Roman wall across northern England
an ace is an expert

explanation.surface: A skilled builder like a Roman emperor became a Scottish hero.
explanation.walkthrough: 'such as Hadrian' points to his wall, not the emperor.
explanation.definitionFit: William Wallace led the Scottish fight for independence against England around 1300.

clue.text: Pick clubs and hearts over diamonds

parts.note: C is the card-suit abbreviation for clubs
H is the card-suit abbreviation for hearts
O is the cricket scorer's abbreviation for an over
ice is slang for diamonds

explanation.surface: A card player selects which suits to play.
explanation.walkthrough: The card-game picture makes 'diamonds' look like a suit abbreviation; it is the slang ICE.
explanation.definitionFit: A pick, as in 'take your pick', is a selection, a synonym.

clue.text: Ancient coat carried during troubles by an aristocratic leader

indicators.note: carried during means the ancient coat is held inside the troubles

parts.note: troubles are harm and ill, two words for misfortune
ancient means old
a mac is a raincoat

explanation.surface: An old coat was worn through hard times by a noble leader.
explanation.walkthrough: 'troubles' has to supply two nouns, HARM and ILL, with nothing in between. 'aristocratic' fits because the 1950s Prime Minister later became an earl.
explanation.definitionFit: The Conservative Prime Minister of 1957 to 1963 became the Earl of Stockton, an aristocratic leader.

clue.text: Trendy joint incorporates, oddly, this design

parts.note: in means fashionable, trendy

indicators.note: incorporates means takes into its body, so the odd letters go inside

parts.note: a tenon is the tongue of a mortise and tenon joint

indicators.note: oddly means the first and third letters of this

explanation.surface: A fashionable carpentry joint built to a set plan.
explanation.definitionFit: Design here means purpose or plan, as in 'by design', a synonym of intention.

clue.text: Source of income apprentice's first lacking

indicators.note: first lacking means without its first letter

parts.note: a learner is an apprentice

explanation.surface: A trainee is short of the first instalment of pay.
explanation.definitionFit: An earner is something that brings in money, as in 'a nice little earner'.

clue.text: Mark replaced roubles? Not right

indicators.note: replaced means put back in a new place, so the letters are reordered
Not says the right letter is excluded

explanation.surface: A currency symbol is changed on some Russian money.
explanation.definitionFit: An obelus is the dagger-shaped printer's mark, or the division sign.

clue.text: Top cop having risen in service, free of imperfection

indicators.note: in places the risen word within the trimmed service
free of says the word for imperfection is taken away from service

parts.note: a vice is a fault or imperfection
having risen means having gone up

explanation.surface: A senior police officer climbed the ranks with a spotless record.
explanation.walkthrough: 'having risen in service' reads like the cop's career, but SER is what 'service' leaves once 'free of' takes away a vice.
explanation.definitionFit: Super is short for superintendent, a senior British police rank, so a top cop.

clue.text: Saviour, I muse, holding book in both hands

indicators.note: in sets the whole run between the letters for the two hands

parts.note: L and R stand for left and right, both hands

indicators.note: holding means the first pair of words wraps around the book

parts.note: Erato is the Muse of lyric poetry

explanation.surface: Someone reflects on a redeemer while clutching a holy book in both hands.
explanation.walkthrough: 'holding' puts B between I and ERATO; 'in' then places that between L and R. 'muse' looks like a verb but is the noun.
explanation.definitionFit: One who frees people, a deliverer, is a saviour: near-synonyms.

clue.text: One's doing a turn before tea in island theatre

indicators.note: in places the run inside the island's name

parts.note: Mull is an island of the Scottish Inner Hebrides

indicators.note: doing a turn says the letters for one's are read backwards

parts.note: one's is I'S, I for one plus S for is
cha is slang for tea

explanation.surface: A performer does a turn before teatime at a Hebridean venue.
explanation.walkthrough: 'doing a turn' sounds like a variety act, apt for the answer, but it reverses IS to SI.
explanation.definitionFit: A music hall is a variety theatre of the Victorian kind, so the answer is a type of theatre.

clue.text: Attack enemy leader after a breather

indicators.note: after puts the leader letter behind the breather

parts.note: a lung is what one breathes with

indicators.note: leader means the first letter of enemy

explanation.surface: After pausing for breath, someone strikes at the head of the opposing side.
explanation.walkthrough: 'a breather' looks like a rest; here it is the organ that breathes.
explanation.definitionFit: A lunge is a sudden forward thrust, a fencing attack: a synonym.

clue.text: Mostly imbibe sort of wine that's sweet

definitions.note: a noun phrase: something that is sweet

indicators.note: Mostly means all but the last letter of the word for imbibe

parts.note: to suck is to imbibe, as through a straw
rosé is a pink sort of wine

explanation.surface: Drinking most of a glass of sweet wine.
explanation.definitionFit: Sucrose is cane or beet sugar, a substance whose defining property is sweetness.

clue.text: Singer wanted peripheral sections cut during church service

indicators.note: during means the trimmed word is placed within church and service

parts.note: a use is a form of liturgical service, as in the Sarum Use

indicators.note: peripheral sections cut means the outside letters of wanted are removed

explanation.surface: A singer was sought for the cut-down sections of a church service.
explanation.definitionFit: A chanteuse is a female singer, especially in a nightclub.

clue.text: Males dressed formally for such a meeting?

indicators.note: dressed means clothed, so the formal outfit goes around the men

parts.note: dressing formally means wearing a suit
M is male, so two Ms for males

explanation.surface: Men in suits and ties for a high-level gathering.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark admits that the whole clue doubles as a picture of the event, since summit delegates usually wear suits.
explanation.definitionFit: A summit is a meeting of heads of government, typically suited men.

clue.text: A small room this paper's editor made bullet-proof?

parts.note: RM is short for room
the newspaper speaking of itself says our

explanation.surface: The editor's small office has been made safe against gunfire.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark flags that armoured means protected against bullets rather than bulletproof itself.
explanation.definitionFit: Armoured vehicles carry steel plating that resists gunfire, so they are bulletproof in effect.

clue.text: I work in medical institution in old city

indicators.note: in puts the I and work letters inside the institution

parts.note: san is short for sanatorium
go means work, as a machine does

explanation.surface: Someone works at a hospital in a historic town.
explanation.definitionFit: Saigon was the former name of Ho Chi Minh City in Vietnam, so an old city name.

clue.text: Steal gold coin bishop preserved

indicators.note: preserved means kept inside, so the bishop goes within the coin

parts.note: the noble was an old English gold coin
B is the chess abbreviation for bishop

explanation.surface: A bishop kept a gold coin safe from thieves.
explanation.definitionFit: Nobble is British slang meaning to steal or pinch.

clue.text: Supplier of breakfast buffet sent outside about lunchtime?

indicators.note: sent outside means the buffet's letters go around the others

parts.note: a buffet is a bar serving refreshments
C is circa, about
one o'clock is lunchtime

explanation.surface: A breakfast caterer has the buffet carried outdoors around lunch.
explanation.walkthrough: 'buffet' could be a blow, but it is the counter, BAR.
explanation.definitionFit: A baconer is a pig fattened for bacon, which supplies the breakfast rasher: a whimsical description.

clue.text: First half of book by fantastic writer

indicators.note: First half of means the opening two letters of book

parts.note: swell means excellent, fantastic

explanation.surface: The opening half of a novel by a brilliant author.
explanation.definitionFit: James Boswell wrote the Life of Samuel Johnson, the most famous biography in English.

clue.text: Small fruit and some asparagus?

parts.note: pears are fruit

explanation.surface: A greengrocer lists small fruit and a bit of asparagus.
explanation.definitionFit: Asparagus is sold as spears, the young shoots, so some asparagus by example.

clue.text: It helps mountaineer no end on way back

indicators.note: on way back says the letters are read in reverse

parts.note: a tip is an end or point

explanation.surface: A climbing aid that is endless when reversed along a route.
explanation.definitionFit: A piton is a metal spike driven into rock as an anchor, gear that assists climbers.

clue.text: Thrashing is not a bad form of punishment

indicators.note: thrashing about means flailing wildly, so these letters are jumbled

explanation.surface: A beating is presented as a not-too-bad sort of penalty.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Thrashing' looks like the definition but signals the anagram.
explanation.definitionFit: A bastinado is a beating on the soles of the feet, an old punishment.

clue.text: Character initially dug out of a hole

indicators.note: out of means the initial letter is taken from the rest

parts.note: a ditch is a hole or trench in the ground

indicators.note: initially means the first letter of dug

explanation.surface: Someone digs their way out of a pit.
explanation.definitionFit: Aitch is the spelt-out name of the letter H, a character of the alphabet.

clue.text: Answer question posh French female artist put about painting technique

parts.note: U means upper-class, posh

indicators.note: put about, as a ship turns, says the letters run backwards

parts.note: RA is a Royal Academician, an artist
elle is French for she

explanation.surface: A Frenchwoman painter is questioned about her method.
explanation.definitionFit: Aquarelle is painting with transparent watercolours, a technique.

clue.text: Corrupt cartel losing capital after a while

indicators.note: corrupt means spoilt or perverted, so the letters are disordered
losing capital means the first letter of cartel is dropped

explanation.surface: A crooked cartel lost its funds in time.
explanation.walkthrough: 'capital' suggests money; it means the first letter, C.
explanation.definitionFit: Later means at a subsequent time, an idiomatic equivalent of after a while.

clue.text: Woman doing a twirl in ballet shoes

indicators.note: doing a twirl says the hidden letters are read backwards
the clue word that says the letters sit inside the next words

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A dancer pirouettes in her ballet shoes.
explanation.definitionFit: Stella is a female given name, so this is a woman's name.

clue.text: Drew back, having dashed across island

indicators.note: across means the dashing word stretches over the island

parts.note: fled means ran off, dashed away
inch is a Scottish word for a small island

explanation.surface: Someone recoiled after racing across an island.
explanation.definitionFit: To flinch is to recoil or wince, a synonym of drew back.
